scope: RP2040 Cortex-M0+ binary64 multiplication and division, compared with the previous owned runtime and external Qfplib-M0-full.

implementation.multiply: Reuse the guarded exponent, pack its sign/bias once, and omit redundant result-range checks. For a zero low significand word, use two exact 32x32 products rather than four; if both low words are zero the low product is also skipped. All rounding and sticky bits are preserved.
implementation.multiply_high_terms: The high significands have at most 21 bits, so the sum of their 16-bit cross terms cannot overflow 32 bits. Only these bounded high products skip the unsigned carry branch.
implementation.divide: Reuse the guarded biased exponent and normal-only unpacking. Quotient refinement multiplies a signed residual |r0x|<2^30 (the residual bound is 26*2^25, well below 2^30) by a reciprocal in [0,2^30]. The signed cross-term sum therefore fits int32_t and needs no separate sign/carry correction.
implementation.sio_latency: Schedule nine independent ALU instructions between DIV_UDIVISOR and DIV_QUOTIENT. The first prototype had only seven and failed physical qualification. The final ARM test rejects that prototype; the corrected code passed physical comparisons and the full mathematical corpus.
implementation.range_proof: Multiply guard admits ea+eb-1024 in [0,2043]; division guard admits ea-eb+1021 in [0,2043]. Either normalization and a rounding carry remain finite normal. Other inputs retain the unchanged full IEEE fallback.
implementation.ieee: Preserve nearest-even, signed zero, subnormal results, infinities and NaNs. An already dirty SIO divider is preserved via the independent software fallback; dyadic-seed and power-of-two paths do not touch SIO.
implementation.license: Existing BSD-3-Clause Pico SDK foundation and project changes. Qfplib GPL-2.0 source is an external separately linked comparison APP and is neither copied nor linked into the firmware.

armv6m.abi: Cortex-M0, soft EABI registers, R4-R11/SP preserved; writes stack and SIO divider only
armv6m.timing_note: Instruction counts are emulator diagnostics, not measured RP2040 cycles.

production_elf_math.abi: Cortex-M0, soft EABI registers, R4-R11/SP preserved; writes stack and SIO divider only
production_elf_math.timing_note: Instruction counts are emulator diagnostics, not measured RP2040 cycles.

unchanged_addition_bytes.scope: Read-only byte comparison: subtraction entry and all addition fast paths in the production ELF exactly match the independently tested ARM binary. No ELF execution or external fallback relocation check is performed.

sio_latency_regression.diagnostic: ('SIO quotient read before eight ALU instructions', 7)

tests.sio_model_scope: Functional divider model, with an eight-ALU schedule check for the owned straight-line reciprocal seed block. SDK callers can use branches or memory operations to wait; their cycles are not modeled.

physical_math.location: Local compact_math and owned arithmetic execute in SRAM; no resident math imports.

tests.map_gate: PASS: no extracted libgcc archive members

conditions.location: OWN, BASE and QFP execute in SRAM without resident arithmetic imports; GCC is the resident Flash control.

limits: Latencies describe the published deterministic inputs. The six-stream means give every stream equal weight, including powers of two and dyadic seeds.
On full-precision ordinary significands Qfplib remains about 2-3 percent faster, and on the short-divisor division stream about 4 percent faster. No universal speed ordering is claimed.
Qfplib comparison streams use finite normal inputs/results; its FTZ/NaN behavior is not timed as if it implemented full IEEE arithmetic.
No new binary32 or non-RP2040 performance claim is made. Cortex-M4 and the portable M0 implementation are unchanged.
The replacement firmware was built and qualified through its ELF. Physical qualification used self-contained SRAM APPs without flashing.
